scenario: The coach has just delivered a week to the provider — three strength sessions and three runs. The athlete asks 都送到手錶了嗎？
given: All six sessions came back accepted by the provider, each with an external id.
The three runs carry structured steps, so the device renders them phase by phase with targets.
The three strength sessions carry a title and a line per movement as text; the provider stores no sets/reps structure for them and no device step is generated.
Nothing in this turn's evidence says how the athlete's watch renders a strength entry — no session has been executed from the watch yet.

expected.conclusion: Provider acceptance is not device rendering, and the two sports did not get the same thing: the runs will be guided step by step, the strength sessions arrive as a title and a line of text per movement. Say that difference plainly rather than answering 都送到了 for all six.
must_state: The runs carry structured steps the watch guides through; the strength sessions carry text only.
Acceptance by the provider proves the entry is on the calendar, not what the watch will show.
How the watch actually renders a strength entry has not been observed here.
must_not_state: That the watch will prompt the athlete set by set through a strength session.
That provider acceptance confirms anything about the device.
That the strength sessions failed to deliver, or were not delivered.

fails_if: The answer covers all six sessions with one 都送到手錶了 and never distinguishes the two sports.
The answer promises set-by-set guidance for strength because the delivery succeeded.
The answer, being unsure about device rendering, omits the strength sessions entirely and leaves the athlete thinking they were not delivered.
The answer treats the missing device observation as a delivery failure rather than as an unknown.
